Accountable obligation owner.value: Operational Risk owns the ICT business continuity policy under DORA Art. 11(1)-(2); Business Continuity Manager authors the plans, Chief Info Security Officer countersigns the ICT content, management body approves under Art. 5(2)

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Arts. 11(1)-(2), 11(6), 12 and 14 read against the EUR-Lex consolidated text, plus Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774 Arts. 24-26 (ICT business continuity policy, response and recovery plans, testing) and Art. 3(22) for the critical-or-important-function definition; re-read at each annual policy review and on any ESA guidance update

In-scope processes.value: Every process supporting a critical or important function of the EU insurance undertaking and its EEA branches - policy administration, claims payment, premium collection, distribution portals, actuarial valuation and regulatory reporting - plus the ICT services underpinning them, including those delivered by intragroup and external ICT third-party providers

In-scope systems.value: Business continuity module holds the CIF inventory, impact tolerances, RTO/RPO per function and the linked plan set; CMDB supplies the ICT asset dependency mapping and the document management repository holds the approved plan PDFs

Compliance procedure documented.value: ICT Business Continuity Policy plus the subordinate ICT Response and Recovery Plan set, Backup and Restoration Standard (Art. 12), Crisis Communication Plan (Art. 14) and third-party Exit Strategy templates (Art. 28(8)), each naming scenario, RTO, RPO, invocation authority and recovery sequence

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the management body (Board Risk Committee then full Board) under DORA Art. 5(2) at least annually; interim changes above the materiality threshold approved by the Chief Risk Officer and ratified at the next Board sitting

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual policy review closes before the Board Risk Committee November sitting so the approved plan set is live from 1 January; plan refresh is also triggered within 30 calendar days of any major ICT-related incident, material outsourcing change or resilience-test failure

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC workflow raises review tasks at T-90, T-45 and T-15 days to the Board Risk Committee papers deadline, and an event-driven task on any incident classified major or any CIF added to the register of information

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Approved plan versions, CIF inventory snapshots, RTO/RPO derivation workings, Board minutes and distribution acknowledgements retained 10 years from supersession to cover the supervisory record-keeping expectation and Solvency II documentation retention

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A CIF with no current plan, a missing or unjustified RTO/RPO, or an unapproved plan version is raised as an operational-resilience issue with root cause, owner, due date and Chief Risk Officer visibility

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Risk Officer signs off closure of every plan-coverage gap and every RTO/RPO breach accepted as a temporary risk, with the acceptance expiry date recorded

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All critical or important functions recorded in the CIF inventory for the EU entity in the review year, each with its supporting ICT assets, third-party dependencies and linked continuity plan

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on coverage - any CIF without an approved, in-date continuity and recovery plan is a fail; RTO/RPO documented but not evidenced by a test result is a fail; more than two fails or any fail on a payment-related CIF escalates to the Board Risk Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is an annual policy review under Art. 6(5)/Art. 11; independent test runs annually ahead of Board approval, with a targeted retest within 60 days of any major ICT-related incident that invoked a plan

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Internal Audit reviewer must not sit in Operational Risk, IT Operations or Business Continuity and must have authored none of the sampled plans

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual ICT business continuity assurance workpaper - CIF population extract, plan-coverage reconciliation, RTO/RPO re-derivation, exception log - filed in the compliance evidence repository under DORA Art. 11

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Plan set, CIF inventory, impact tolerance rationale, last test results and Board approval minutes assembled as a supervisory pack deliverable to the national competent authority within 10 business days of request

Regulator response path.value: Compliance coordinates the response to the national competent authority (and EIOPA where the request is ESA-led); General Counsel clears any statement acknowledging an uncovered critical function before it leaves the firm

checklist.step: Fix the DORA entity scope and proportionality position
actions: List every EU-authorised insurance and reinsurance undertaking, EEA branch and intermediary in the group and record each one's LEI and its national competent authority.

For each entity decide whether the simplified ICT risk management framework under DORA Art. 16 applies (small and non-interconnected undertakings) or the full Art. 5-15 framework; record the headcount, balance-sheet and gross-premium figures the call rests on.
Ask the Regulatory Reporting Manager for the latest Solvency II entity list so no in-scope legal entity is missed.
Open a scoping record in the GRC business continuity module for each in-scope entity and attach the scoping memo.
checklist.done: every EU legal entity has a recorded DORA scoping decision, an LEI, a named competent authority and an attached rationale.

checklist.step: Rebuild the critical or important function inventory against the Art. 3(22) definition
actions: Take the business service catalogue from the Operations Manager and test each service against DORA Art. 3(22): would disruption materially impair financial performance, or the soundness or continuity of the authorised services and activities.

Retain as CIFs at minimum claims settlement and payment, premium collection, policy issuance, customer contact handling, actuarial reserving, investment settlement and regulatory reporting; record a written reason for anything excluded.
Have the Chief Operating Officer and Chief Risk Officer challenge and confirm the list in a documented workshop before it is frozen.
Load the confirmed list into the GRC CIF register with function owner, entity, LEI and the confirmation date.
checklist.done: the CIF register holds a dated, Chief Risk Officer-confirmed entry per function with an Art. 3(22) rationale, including exclusions.

checklist.step: Set impact tolerance, RTO and RPO for each critical or important function
actions: Run a business impact analysis per CIF with the function owner: quantify loss per hour of outage, policyholder detriment, regulatory reporting breach points and the maximum tolerable period of disruption.
Convert the maximum tolerable period into a recovery time objective and set a recovery point objective from the acceptable data-loss window, in hours, per CIF.
Cross-check the RTO against externally driven deadlines the Regulatory Reporting Manager supplies - Solvency II QRT submission dates, claims payment service standards, direct debit collection cycles.
Record the RTO, RPO, tolerance figure and the workings in the GRC CIF record; anything left blank blocks plan approval.
checklist.done: every CIF carries a quantified impact tolerance, an RTO and an RPO in hours with the business impact analysis attached.

checklist.step: Map each function to its ICT assets, data and third-party dependencies
actions: In the CMDB open each CIF's business service and walk the downstream relationships to applications, databases, middleware, network segments and hosting locations.
Tag every configuration item that supports a CIF with the CIF identifier so the dependency is queryable rather than described in prose.
Take the ICT third-party provider list from the Third-Party Risk Manager and attach the provider, contract reference and service to each supporting configuration item.
Flag single points of failure - one data centre, one provider, one specialist engineer - and hand the list to the Business Continuity Manager for scenario design.
checklist.done: each CIF resolves in the CMDB to a tagged asset chain with named third-party providers and a documented single-point-of-failure list.

checklist.step: Update the ICT business continuity policy to Art. 11 and RTS 2024/1774
actions: Open the current ICT Business Continuity Policy and redline it clause by clause against DORA Art. 11(1)-(2) and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774 Arts. 24-26.

Ensure the policy states the objectives, the CIF scope, the governance and invocation authority, the link to the ICT risk management framework and the requirement to keep the plans separate from and independent of the primary ICT infrastructure.
Add the Art. 11(6) obligation to record all activities before, during and after a disruption in a way that reconstructs the timeline.
Circulate the redline to the Chief Info Security Officer and Compliance Officer for comment and log every comment and its disposition in the review sheet.
Save the clean version as a new numbered release in the document management repository with the DORA article mapping table appended.
checklist.done: a redlined-to-clean policy release exists with an article-by-article mapping to Art. 11 and RTS 2024/1774 Arts. 24-26 and disposed reviewer comments.

checklist.step: Write the ICT response and recovery plans per scenario
actions: Build a plan per severe-but-plausible scenario: data-centre loss, ransomware encryption of policy and claims data, cloud region failure, loss of the core policy administration provider, and loss of a critical payment interface.
For each scenario write the invocation trigger, the invocation authority by name and deputy, the recovery sequence by system, and the manual workaround the business runs while ICT recovers.
State the recovery sequence in the order the CIFs need it - payments and claims before reporting - and reference the RTO figure on each step.
Name the resources required per step: engineers on the call tree, standby infrastructure, provider hotline numbers and contract reference for the recovery commitment.
Hand each draft to the function owner for confirmation that the workaround is actually operable at the stated volumes.
checklist.done: each severe-but-plausible scenario has an owned plan with invocation trigger, named authority, RTO-sequenced recovery steps and a business-confirmed workaround.

checklist.step: Set the backup and restoration arrangements required by Art. 12
actions: Define per CIF data set the backup scope, frequency and retention consistent with the RPO, and record the backup method in the backup standard.
Confirm backups are physically and logically segregated from the source system, with at least one immutable or offline copy that ransomware cannot reach from the production identity domain.
Specify the restoration and recovery procedures, including the use of an isolated restoration environment so restores never overwrite production during verification.
Set the periodic restore-test cadence and record who performs it and where the result is filed.
Have the Chief Info Security Officer confirm the segregation design in writing before the standard is published.
checklist.done: a published backup and restoration standard states scope, frequency, retention, segregation, immutable copy and restore-test cadence for each CIF data set.

checklist.step: Build the crisis management and communication plan required by Art. 14
actions: Write the crisis communication plan naming the person accountable for disclosure to clients, financial counterparts and the public, and the deputy.

Draft holding statements for policyholders, brokers and distributors covering an outage, a data compromise and a payment delay, and get them pre-cleared by General Counsel and the Communications Specialist.
Set the internal escalation ladder with time triggers from detection to crisis-team convening and to management-body notification.

Add the Art. 11(10) route for informing clients without undue delay where a major ICT-related incident has or may have an impact on their financial interests, and name the channel used for each client segment.
Store the call tree and the statements outside the primary ICT estate so they survive the outage they cover.
checklist.done: a crisis communication plan exists with a named accountable person, pre-cleared statements, time-triggered escalation and an out-of-band copy.

checklist.step: Attach exit strategies and alternative solutions for the ICT providers behind each CIF
actions: For every ICT third-party service supporting a CIF, open the contract in the CLM repository and read the termination, transition assistance and data return clauses.
Write the DORA Art. 28(8) exit strategy: trigger events, the alternative provider or in-house option, the data extraction format and volume, the transition duration estimate and the cost owner.
Confirm the exit can be executed without disrupting the CIF and without breaching the RTO, and state the assumption that supports that claim.
Where no viable alternative exists, log a concentration risk issue for the Chief Risk Officer rather than writing an aspirational exit plan.
Link the exit strategy document to the contract record and to the CIF record in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: every CIF-supporting ICT contract has a linked exit strategy naming the alternative, the data extraction route and the transition duration, or a logged concentration risk.

checklist.step: Wire the plan set into the ICT risk management framework
actions: Create a control record in the GRC platform for each Art. 11, 12 and 14 requirement and link it to the policy clause and the evidence artefact that satisfies it.
Map the continuity controls to the ICT risk register entries for availability, integrity and third-party concentration so risk owners see the mitigations.
Set control testing frequency and the responsible tester on each record so the annual assurance run has a defined scope.
Run the module's completeness report and clear any control with no linked evidence before publishing.
checklist.done: every Art. 11/12/14 requirement has a GRC control record linked to policy clause, evidence and a named tester, with no unlinked controls.

checklist.step: Take the plan set to the management body for approval under Art. 5(2)
actions: Prepare the Board Risk Committee paper: CIF list with RTO/RPO, changes since last approval, open gaps with owners and dates, last test results and the residual risk statement.
Load the paper and the policy release to the board portal ahead of the papers deadline and record the distribution date.
At the sitting capture the decision, any conditions attached and the review period the management body sets.
Minute the approval with the exact policy version number so the approved artefact is unambiguous.
Publish the approved version and notify the Chief Risk Officer, Chief Info Security Officer and function owners.
checklist.done: board minutes record approval of a named policy version with conditions and the next review date, and the approved version is published.

checklist.step: Assign plan roles and train the people who will execute them
actions: Extract every named role from the plans - invocation authority, recovery leads, communications lead, provider liaison - and confirm a current post-holder and a deputy for each.
Assign the ICT continuity awareness module in the learning management system to all named post-holders with a 30-day completion deadline.
Run a walkthrough session per plan with the named team so they have read their own steps before an event, and record attendance.
Chase non-completions weekly and escalate anyone still outstanding after 45 days to their function owner.
checklist.done: every named plan role has a current holder and deputy with recorded training completion and walkthrough attendance.

checklist.step: Publish, version-control and distribute the plans so they survive the outage
actions: Publish each plan with a version number, effective date, owner and approval reference on the cover page.
Retire the superseded versions to a read-only archive so no team can invoke a stale plan.
Produce an offline copy set - printed or on encrypted removable media held at the alternate site - because the repository itself may be unavailable during invocation.
Record the distribution list and collect acknowledgements from each recipient.
checklist.done: the current plan set is published, superseded versions archived read-only, an offline copy exists at the alternate site and acknowledgements are recorded.

checklist.step: Arm the annual and event-driven review triggers
actions: Create the annual review task in the GRC platform dated to close before the Board Risk Committee papers deadline, with T-90, T-45 and T-15 reminders.

Add event triggers that open a review task automatically on: any incident classified major under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772, any new or terminated CIF-supporting ICT contract, any failed resilience test, and any supervisory instruction.
Name the reviewer and approver on each trigger so an unassigned task cannot sit idle.
Report open review tasks past due in the monthly operational risk pack.
checklist.done: an annual review task with reminders plus four named event triggers exist in the GRC platform with assigned reviewers.

checklist.step: Assemble and retain the supervisory evidence pack
actions: File in the compliance evidence repository under DORA Art. 11: the approved policy version, the CIF register extract, business impact analyses, plan set, backup standard, exit strategies, training records and board minutes.
Apply a 10-year-from-supersession retention label so the record outlives the plan version.
Index the pack by legal entity, LEI and CIF so a competent authority request can be answered by query rather than by search.
Run a retrieval test - pull the full pack for one entity and time it - and record the elapsed time against the 10-business-day commitment.
checklist.done: a retention-labelled, entity-indexed evidence pack exists and a timed retrieval test proves the 10-business-day commitment.

testing.step: Build the population of critical or important functions for the review year
actions: Extract the CIF register from the GRC business continuity module for every in-scope EU entity, with function name, entity LEI, owner, RTO, RPO and linked plan reference.
Add any function flagged as supporting a critical or important function in the DORA register of information so the two records cannot diverge unnoticed.
Reconcile the extract to the business service catalogue held by the Operations Manager and resolve every difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date, record count and the query used.
testing.done: the CIF population is reconciled to the service catalogue and the register of information, and signed as complete with a reproducible query.

testing.step: Reconcile every function to an approved, in-date plan
actions: Match each population row to a published plan version in the document management repository on CIF identifier.
Check the plan's approval reference traces to a board or Board Risk Committee minute and that the approval date is inside the last 12 months.
List any CIF with no plan, a draft-status plan, or an approval older than 12 months as an automatic exception with no judgement applied.
Confirm the superseded versions are archived read-only so an invocation cannot pick up a stale plan.
testing.done: every CIF is matched to an approved plan version dated within 12 months, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of CIFs involving policyholder payments, claims settlement or regulatory reporting.
Take 10 further CIFs by seeded random selection from the remainder, for a minimum of 15 sampled functions.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and the inclusion rule in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Note any CIF added to the register after the extract date and treat it as a subsequent-events item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all payment, claims and reporting functions plus a seeded random remainder.

testing.step: Re-derive the RTO and RPO for each sampled function
actions: Read the business impact analysis behind each sampled CIF and re-derive the maximum tolerable period of disruption from the stated loss-per-hour and detriment figures without first reading the recorded RTO.
Compare your derived RTO and RPO to the recorded values; any difference greater than 25% or any value with no supporting analysis is an exception.

Check the RTO against the externally fixed deadlines - Solvency II QRT dates, direct debit collection cycles, claims payment service standards - and flag any RTO that would still breach an external deadline.
Attach the recomputation sheet to the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled CIF has an independent RTO/RPO re-derivation with differences and unsupported values logged.

testing.step: Trace the dependency mapping into the CMDB and the third-party register
actions: In the CMDB query the configuration items tagged to each sampled CIF and compare the returned asset chain to the plan's stated recovery sequence.
Confirm every ICT third-party provider named in the asset chain appears in the register of information with a contract reference.
Identify any asset in the recovery sequence that is absent from the CMDB, and any tagged asset absent from the plan - both are exceptions.
Capture the CMDB dependency view into the workpaper for each sampled CIF.
testing.done: the CMDB asset chain, the plan recovery sequence and the third-party register agree for each sampled CIF or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Test the backup and restoration arrangements against Art. 12
actions: For each sampled CIF data set read the backup job configuration and compare the actual backup frequency to the RPO on the CIF record.
Verify at least one copy is logically segregated or immutable and cannot be deleted from the production identity domain, by inspecting the retention-lock or offline-media evidence.
Obtain the most recent restore-test result and confirm the restore ran into an isolated environment, completed within the RTO and validated data integrity.
Where no restore test exists in the last 12 months, record a fail regardless of the backup configuration quality.
testing.done: backup frequency reconciles to the RPO, an immutable or segregated copy is evidenced and a restore test within 12 months met the RTO.

testing.step: Verify the exit strategies behind sampled third-party dependencies
actions: Pull the exit strategy for each ICT provider supporting a sampled CIF and read it against DORA Art. 28(8).
Confirm the contract clauses in the CLM repository actually grant the transition assistance, data return format and notice period the exit strategy assumes.
Test that a named alternative provider or in-house option exists and that the stated transition duration is shorter than the tolerance for disruption of that CIF.
Treat an exit strategy that assumes contractual rights the agreement does not contain as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled provider exit strategy is supported by matching contract clauses, a named alternative and a transition duration inside the tolerance.

testing.step: Recompute the review-cycle and approval timing arithmetic
actions: For each sampled plan compute the elapsed days between the previous approval date and the current approval date and confirm it does not exceed 365.
Identify every major ICT-related incident, failed resilience test and material ICT contract change in the year, and confirm a plan review opened within 30 calendar days of each.
Check the GRC event triggers actually fired by inspecting the task history, not by reading the configuration.
Log any review that opened late with the number of days late.
testing.done: annual review intervals are within 365 days and every event trigger produced a review task within 30 days, with lateness quantified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception stating the CIF, the requirement missed, the DORA article and the resilience impact.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list - CIF not identified, impact analysis not refreshed, plan not approved, dependency not mapped, restore test not run, exit right absent - plus a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a payment or claims CIF is uncovered, open an immediate interim workaround alongside the fix.
Carry every open exception forward as a mandatory retest row in next year's assurance scope.
testing.done: each exception has an issue record, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the coverage exception rate and compare it to the zero-tolerance plan-coverage threshold.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - naming the evidence references behind each judgement.
Have the reviewer, who sits outside Operational Risk, IT Operations and Business Continuity and authored no sampled plan, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and open exceptions to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and a Board Risk Committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.
